articles.hed: Arrowhead Statement: Walker III 173 Rush as Chiefs Beat Broncos 31–10
articles.deck: Mahomes back from ACL; KWIII steals the show. Bears still riding 59–37 opener into Vikings at home.
articles.body: On Monday Night Football, Kenneth Walker III debuted for Kansas City with 173 rushing yards and two touchdowns in a 31–10 win over Denver. Patrick Mahomes returned from ACL surgery with 184 pass yards, two passing TDs, and a rushing score; Bo Nix and the Broncos managed just 176 total yards. Chicago’s 59–37 franchise-opener demolition of Carolina still echoes — Soldier Field hosts Minnesota this Sunday. Carry that tempo into the Opening Bell.

articles.hed: AI Desk: Siri AI Ships; Hooks for Claude/ChatGPT Surface; xAI Drops Apple Suit
articles.deck: English beta live; private Model Delegation code; X/SpaceXAI dismiss Apple claims but keep OpenAI in the case.
articles.body: Apple’s Siri AI rolled out Monday in English beta with iOS/iPadOS 27-era software. AppleInsider found private hooks that can swap or extend Siri’s backend toward Claude or ChatGPT — not yet public. Separately, X Corp and SpaceXAI dismissed antitrust claims against Apple over ChatGPT integration while continuing the case against OpenAI. Full desks below.

items.hed: The Veil Is a Filter, Not a Wall
items.body: Gnostic teachers spoke of the veil between the apparent world and the real as something that thins with attention — not a brick barrier. Tuesday’s storms are noise on the screen; the charge underneath is still yours. Practice seeing the filter for what it is: weather, inbox, feed — then choose what passes through.

Classical Hermetica pairs the elements: water dissolves form; fire concentrates will. A wet forecast is not a soft day unless you let it be. Keep the inner fire (breath, plank, next clear move) while the outer water does its work. Coherence under weather is the real alchemy.

In esoteric practice, to name a force is to place it. Name the morning: charge, body, security skim, then the rest. Unnamed urgency owns you; named urgency becomes a task with a place on the page. Forbidden knowledge, stripped of theater, is often just precise naming.

items.hed: Siri AI is here — English beta with next-gen Apple Intelligence
items.body: Apple said Siri AI launched Monday as a more capable, conversational assistant with personal context, world knowledge, onscreen awareness, and deeper app actions. Rollout starts in English; French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish are due next month across the 2027 software releases.

items.hed: iOS 27 code shows Siri AI can be swapped for Claude or ChatGPT
items.body: Private hooks in iOS 27 / macOS Golden Gate betas reveal Model Delegation and Inference Providing paths that can run Claude as a Siri extension or replace Siri’s server model with ChatGPT — demos exist, but the features are not enabled for regular users yet.

items.hed: X Corp and SpaceXAI drop antitrust claims against Apple; OpenAI case continues
items.body: Elon Musk’s X and SpaceXAI dismissed their Apple antitrust claims Monday without explaining why. The suit had accused Apple of favoring ChatGPT in iOS; claims against OpenAI remain active.

items.hed: Altman backs Amodei’s ‘pace the frontier’ — independent evaluators, federal safety frame
items.body: OpenAI’s Sam Altman welcomed a federal safety framework after aligning with Anthropic’s Dario Amodei and Elon Musk on slowing capability races so safety can keep up. Altman backed independent evaluators with employee-like access; pacing is not a stop, he said.

items.hed: Raptors complete Kawhi Leonard trade from Clippers after NBA probe
items.body: Toronto finalized the Kawhi Leonard deal Monday after pausing it during the salary-cap investigation. In exchange, the Raptors sent Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round picks, a first-round swap, and two second-rounders to L.A.

items.hed: Leonard returns to Toronto; media day expected Sept. 28
items.body: After the NBA approved the trade, Kawhi is officially a Raptor again. The league had fined him $700k but did not suspend him or void his deal; he is expected to speak at Toronto’s media day on Sept. 28.

items.hed: Ballmer’s acceptance of sanctions clears a path for Clippers to move on
items.body: Steve Ballmer apologized and said L.A. will comply with the NBA’s historic penalties — $30M fine, five forfeited first-rounders (2029–33), and his one-year suspension — after the Kawhi-related cap probe. Analysts say stopping the fight was the franchise’s best path forward.

items.hed: Walker III’s dazzling debut leads Chiefs past Broncos 31–10
items.body: Kenneth Walker III rushed for 173 yards and scored twice in his Chiefs debut as Kansas City beat Denver on MNF. Patrick Mahomes returned from ACL surgery with 184 pass yards, two pass TDs, and a rushing score; Denver managed 176 total yards.

items.hed: Bears still buzzing after franchise-opener record 59–37 win
items.body: Caleb Williams (269 pass / 65 rush, four total TDs), D’Andre Swift (124, 3 TDs), and Kyle Monangai (100, 1 TD) powered 552 yards in Charlotte. Next: Minnesota at Soldier Field for the home opener.

items.hed: Broncos call 31–10 loss ‘disappointing’; home opener vs. Jaguars next
items.body: Sean Payton’s side pointed to early turnovers, missed chances after a deep pick, and Walker’s 60-yard fourth-down TD. Bo Nix had an INT and a lost fumble; Denver hosts Jacksonville Sunday.

items.hed: Aspinall vacates UFC heavyweight title amid ongoing eye issues
items.body: Tom Aspinall relinquished the heavyweight belt Monday after further right-eye damage delayed his return from the Gane eye-poke no-contest. He is not retiring; Ciryl Gane is expected to be elevated to undisputed champion.

items.hed: Benn confronts future after Garcia’s two-round stoppage
items.body: After Ryan Garcia retained the WBC welterweight title by stopping Conor Benn in round two in Las Vegas, Benn said he does not yet know what’s next — a move back up in weight is the likely path when he returns.

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the rest of the board.

mindset.body: Dom does not wait for clear skies to start. Fierce calm is competitive composure when the radar is loud: charge first, body second, security skim when ready, admin only after the morning has already won. One breath, one move, one clear next step. Competitors may arrive loud; he arrives prepared. When pressure rises, he slows the breath, names the next action, and outlasts the noise. Today is not about proving anything. It is about starting clean so the rest of the week has room to land.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time. Optional: Front Clips / Back Clips if you want a second RipStick move.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.hed: Establish Your Steps Before You Run
grimoire.body: “The heart of man plans his way, but the Lord establishes his steps.” (Proverbs 16:9) Solomon’s counsel is not against planning — it is against rushing an unestablished plan. A Tuesday that opens with charge and body establishes the steps; the inbox and the radar become secondary weather. Classical lore cast Solomon as one who ordered the court before the petition. Order the morning the same way — breath first, body second, then the board.
grimoire.practice: Finish Opening Bell and the 3-minute opener before any security skim. Establish the step; then walk it.

techDemo.kicker: Fast learn · from your X bookmarks
techDemo.pick: SpaceXAI engineer Lauren Tan — GrokBot as a team (Chief of Staff → Managers → Workers), not one chat window
techDemo.author: @Dmytroo_eth

image.alt: GrokBot org chart — Chief of Staff to Managers to Workers to autonomous workflow

lesson.oneLiner: Stop living in one chat. Promote the work: Chief of Staff routes → Managers own lanes → Workers execute → Skills + workflows run overnight.
beats: Chief of Staff = the router that prioritizes and assigns (not the doer of every task).
Managers = 3 lane owners who keep context and hand off clean jobs.
Workers = specialists that actually ship research / build / launch pieces.
Skills + autonomous workflows = the glue so accepted work keeps moving without you babysitting.
Tan’s punchline: 20+ agents organized beats one mega-thread wondering why everything is slow.
lesson.takeaway: Under a minute: if you’re still one window deep, spend one evening standing up CoS → Managers → Workers — then Research → Build → Launch → Improve.
